title: Level 4 (Expert) - D-16
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 4♠. The contract is in danger because West's 2♥ overcall makes it very likely that the ♥A is sitting over the ♥K. South can almost guarantee the contract by playing along elimination lines as long as he makes the unusual play of allowing West's ♦K to win the first trick.

West switches to clubs (a trump shift is actually best) and dummy wins the ♣A. The ♦A is cashed for a club discard. By trading a diamond loser (which West won) for a club loser (which East would win), South ensures that East is never able to gain the lead in clubs. If East had been able to gain the lead, a heart lead through South's ♥K would lead to the defeat of the contract.

South continues by ruffing a club high in order to start eliminating that suit. South crosses to the dummy by overtaking a middle spade with the ♠K and ruffs another club high. South crosses again in trump in order to lead dummy's last club. If East discards on this trick, South can discard a heart, allowing West to win the trick. West will be endplayed into either leading away from the ♥A or leading a diamond to concede a ruff and discard.

If East follows to the fourth round of clubs, South must ruff high (this line also works if West has club length). South can then cross to the dummy in spades and lead a heart with the intention of playing the ♥10 if East follows small. When East plays the ♥Q or ♥J, South covers with the ♥K and West wins the ♥A. Regardless of how East plays, West will be endplayed into either giving South a heart trick or surrendering a ruff and discard.
